mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to equity valuations, thereby lowering the present value of future cash flows and pushing S&P 500 prices higher in the near term.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS staying above 4% for >30 days, or the 20-day IC is below -0.05 with p < 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5% in a month following a rate hike, investors anticipate continued price pressures, causing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days to turn negative as deflation expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.5% and previous FEDFUNDS was raised
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when trigger is met, or IC > 0.02 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (labor market additions) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, prompting equity risk-on flows and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-way ANOVA over 5 years of data, or 20-day returns are not positive when trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in INDPRO (production momentum) above +2% signals supply-side strength that outpaces demand, lowering valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >70% of months with INDPRO acceleration, or IC > 0.10 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) falls by more than 5% in a quarter, it indicates weakening consumer demand, which elevates risk aversion and drives negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during qualifying quarters, or IC > 0.05 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive declines in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -1% for two months create expectations of tighter policy, which compresses equity valuations and yields positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when trigger is met, or IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A regime where UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months while PAYEMS shows no significant decline indicates a labor market in equilibrium, producing no predictable equity signal (neutral effect) over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in this regime, or interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP momentum) exceeds 2% above trend, it reflects robust demand for goods and services, which elevates equity risk appetite and produces positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 6-month MA of GDPC1 > +2% above 12-month trend line
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not positive in >80% of months with trigger activation, or IC < -0.10 over the horizon.
